description: Conformance corpus for rendering a `typeRef`. Every generator that turns a type reference into text asserts against this file, so the two cannot drift apart — and, more to the point, cannot drift together.
notes: `typegen` and `docgen` are two resolvers of one grammar. When the array-of-union precedence bug shipped, both were wrong in the same way, so a test asserting only that they AGREE would have passed. Each case therefore pins the expected text explicitly.

`typescript` is what `typegen` emits and what `docgen` puts inside its fenced TypeScript signature. `markdown` is what `docgen` puts in a parameter or field table, where type names are backticked and pipes are escaped for the table.
An element type that is a union or an optional must be parenthesised before `[]`: `string | number[]` is a union with an array, not an array of a union. It compiles, which is why it went unnoticed.

cases.name: an array of a union is parenthesised
an array of an optional is parenthesised
a union of arrays keeps each element unparenthesised
